useful antiadenovirus therapies apparent clinical success in the treatment of severe adenovirus_disease_lex is limited to a few case reports and small series experience is greatest with intravenous ribavirin_lex for documented severe adenovirus_disease_lex two patients developed adenovirus hemorrhagic cystitis after cardiac and bone marrow transplants respectively the bone marrow transplant remaining three children died of adenovirus_disease_lex intravenous ribavirin_lex therapy was well tolerated use of cidofovir_lex in one child was associated with progressive_renal_failure_lex and transplant recipients neonates and children with immunodeficiency_lex although intravenous ribavirin_lex was not effective for all children with severe adenovirus_disease_lex in this series or in the adenovirus_disease_lex may permit earlier antiviral treatment and better evaluation of therapeutic response conclusions two of five children with severe adenovirus_disease_lex treated with intravenous ribavirin_lex recovered the availability of newer rapid diagnostic techniques such as polymerase chain reaction may make earlier more effective treatment of adenovirus_infection_lex possible given the seriousness and increasing prevalence of adenovirus_disease_lex in certain hosts especially children a large multicenter clinical trial of potentially useful antiadenoviral therapies such as intravenous ribavirin_lex is clearly required to demonstrate the most effective and least toxic therapy
